races.name: Happy Retirement Martin Stoneman Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Food For Thought
runners_data.comment: Well bred by a top yard and bred to relish a step up in trip, Food For Thought left a fair impression when fourth at Chepstow last time — that run clearly had more in it. A course trainer with a strong record and a pedigree built for distance make this a compelling threat, though experience so far is limited.

runners_data.name: Hatta Romance
runners_data.comment: A decent fifth on debut at Newbury in a competitive novice, Hatta Romance shaped with encouragement and should improve stepping up in distance — she's bred for 10f and beyond and handles good to soft. Only one start to go on, but the profile suggests more to come.

runners_data.name: Velvet Vega
runners_data.comment: Third on her latest start at Kempton, Velvet Vega flattened out late over an extended trip but her debut form has been well advertised at Group level since — this ought to be a more suitable test back at a sharper distance. Trainer firing at 28% and our top-rated runner here; the concern is she has yet to get her head in front.

races.name: Martin Stonemans Lucky Last Handicap

runners_data.name: Two Plus Two
runners_data.note: Won twice at 14f on good ground and brings strong course credentials over this trip; Pat Cosgrave partners a horse whose recent form (1-4-1 pattern) and front-running profile make them the natural pace-setter here, though the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence if the race somehow doesn't set up for them.|
runners_data.comment: Two Plus Two has a pair of wins in its last five starts, including a one-and-a-half-length success at Bath, and ran to a similar level with every chance when fourth last time from the same mark — same mark again today. Wears first-time blinkers and takes the lead from the front, effective over 10-14f on a sound surface; the mark may be stretching the limits, but this is a weak field.

runners_data.name: Nymphaea
runners_data.note: Second at 12f on soft and third at 16f on standard are encouraging staying credentials for this 4-year-old; Marco Ghiani rides for J Candlish who has been in decent 14-day form (3/25), and Nymphaea's hold-up style suits a race where a lone pacesetter may leave a clear target to chase.|
runners_data.comment: First-time headgear (p) applied as Nymphaea reverts from all-weather to turf, and her last run — a runner-up effort in a classified race at Windsor — showed she can hold her own at this level over the shorter trip. Effective at 12f on the all-weather and still without a win in recent starts, she needs to translate that consistency into a clear run; capable of making a race of it.

runners_data.name: Star Of Jupiter
runners_data.note: Has placed three times in its last five runs including a second at 14f on standard ground, showing genuine staying ability; though mapped to midfield due to the volume of hold-up horses in this field, Harry Davies will likely find Star Of Jupiter settling at the rear as is natural, and the lack of genuine pace makes a late challenge harder to land.|
runners_data.comment: Star Of Jupiter has been below her best in recent starts, beaten nine lengths at Yarmouth last time — a performance that needs to be put behind her. She stays well at up to 17f and acts on a wide range of surfaces, so the conditions are not the issue; first-time eye-shields (etb) may help but a turnaround is needed to get involved.

runners_data.name: Muhib
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (three thirds in five runs) at 12f, stepping up to 1m6f where the extra distance is a question mark; Warren Fentiman rides for a trainer with a modest 14-day strike rate (0/2), and like Star Of Jupiter, Muhib's true hold-up nature means it is shown further forward on the map than it will actually race — dependent on Two Plus Two setting a strong enough gallop.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer at this level without breaking through, Muhib has registered two thirds and two fourths in recent outings and matched that level again when beaten two and a quarter lengths at Doncaster last time — effective over 10-12f and comfortable on today's going. Yet to win in recent starts and clearly exposed, but reliable enough to be in the mix for a placing.

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — no tactical analysis applicable; their absence further reduces the field to four effective runners and removes a potential pace influence or positional complication from the race.|

races.paceDynamic: Two Plus Two is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this five-runner field and, with no challenger likely to press them hard over 1m6f on good ground at Nottingham, they should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. The three hold-up types — Nymphaea, Star Of Jupiter, and Muhib — will be strung out behind, while Regally Blonde is a non-runner, leaving a thin field with little tactical complexity. Because Star Of Jupiter and Muhib are genuine rear-runners whose redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the lack of true midfield types rather than their natural instincts, they will likely settle further back than shown and face a longer closing run than ideal. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting an honest but uncontested tempo over a staying trip — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or sustain a long run from mid-division, with true hold-up horses needing a strong pace to reel in Two Plus Two, which they are unlikely to get.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Two Plus Two Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Two Plus Two controls the pace unchallenged and the tempo stays honest but never brutal over the 1m6f trip.
scenarios.body: If Two Plus Two controls the pace unchallenged and the tempo stays honest but never brutal over the 1m6f trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Nymphaea Runs Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Two Plus Two sets a strong enough pace that Nymphaea, tracking closer than usual, has the fuel to overhaul them near the line.
scenarios.body: If Two Plus Two sets a strong enough pace that Nymphaea, tracking closer than usual, has the fuel to overhaul them near the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong early and Star Of Jupiter or Muhib get a true strong-run race that sets up a finishing burst.
scenarios.body: If the pace is surprisingly strong early and Star Of Jupiter or Muhib get a true strong-run race that sets up a finishing burst.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Messy Race
scenarios.trigger: If Two Plus Two is slow away or checks early, creating a positional scramble that upsets the race pattern entirely.
scenarios.body: If Two Plus Two is slow away or checks early, creating a positional scramble that upsets the race pattern entirely.

watchPoints.text: Two Plus Two's ability to control pace unopposed is the single biggest factor — watch whether Pat Cosgrave elects to stride on boldly or tries to conserve energy, as the tempo Two Plus Two sets will determine whether hold-up horses can close.

Star Of Jupiter and Muhib are genuine hold-up horses shown in midfield on the map due to field composition — watch their actual starting position as both are likely to settle near the rear, making their closing task longer than the race shape map implies.

Nymphaea's last five runs include soft and standard ground rather than good, so watch the going report updates closely — any drying-out through the morning session could subtly affect their effectiveness as a closing force.

With Regally Blonde a non-runner, this is effectively a four-horse race — watch market moves on Nymphaea as the most likely horse to track Two Plus Two and benefit from even a slight pace injection in the final quarter-mile.

races.name: Cambion Electronics 65 Years In Manufacturing 'Hands And Heels' Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Rusheen Boy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won twice recently including off this mark; uncontested lead on Good ground at Nottingham over a stamina trip suits his style, with J&S Birkett showing 2/9 in the past 14 days — primary pace-setter and structurally advantaged by the race shape he will create.
runners_data.comment: Landed a two-length success at Yarmouth last time but largely did so without being tested too hard against modest opposition — revised mark looks like it demands more on that evidence. Effective 6-8f on a sound surface and trainer in decent form; first-time headgear (t) is a plus, but our figures put him well towards the bottom of the field.

runners_data.name: My Boy Harry
runners_data.note: In solid recent form (1-3-3) and handles Good ground well; naturally prominent-styled, likely to sit just off Rusheen Boy and is well-positioned to pounce if the leader weakens — has won at 7f and 8f on similar going, making this a realistic trip.
runners_data.comment: Returning to winning form with first-time blinkers, My Boy Harry ran to form back up in trip when third most recently, three lengths off the pace from a 64 mark — 1lb lower here. He took a handicap at Lingfield three starts back with a bit in hand off a lower mark and looks ready to go close again if building on that; a key danger for our selection.

runners_data.name: Mariner
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who showed a useful 2nd at 8f on Good last time; trainer J Candlish quietly ticking over (1/17 in 14 days) and headgear (tp) suggests connections are trying to sharpen focus — needs to improve on recent form strings showing 7s and 8s but the Going suits.
runners_data.comment: Out of sorts in recent starts with back-to-back poor efforts, Mariner did post a runner-up showing earlier in the year and is clearly capable enough when things go right — tongue-tie applied for the first time today. Probably best at 8-10f on a quick surface and today's conditions suit; the switch in headgear could prompt a bounce-back, though recent form makes it hard to be confident.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 90 days off with no similar-going recent form and a string of sixth-place finishes on Standard; the lengthy absence and lack of Good-ground evidence make it difficult to see where the improvement comes from in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Returning after a 90-day break, Bajan Bandit ran well below form on his most recent start — that effort came over an extended trip and the mark has been easing since. Suited to 7-8f on the all-weather, this is his first start since that disappointing run and on his earlier turf form he can't be dismissed; the question is fitness having been off for three months.

runners_data.name: Mbappe
runners_data.note: 141 days since last run is a significant fitness query; naturally a hold-up horse who won on Standard at 8f, but Good ground form is limited and a race likely to be run at a controlled pace does not serve a closer who needs pace to close into — Hope Regan's 7lb claim helps the weight.
runners_data.comment: Back after 141 days off, Mbappe was a bit keen in cheekpieces at Kempton last time and beaten four and a quarter lengths — the break since then is a significant unknown. Effective 7-8f on a sound surface and on a fair mark, but returning from a long lay-off and now sporting first-time headgear (p); too much to take on trust at this stage.

runners_data.name: Volendam
runners_data.note: AWCarroll's four-year-old has won and placed on Good ground at 8f and brings strong similar-going credentials (2/15 including a win and a place); a natural prominent horse placed into midfield on the map because the front positions are taken, meaning he will likely travel a touch wider or deeper than ideal, which tempers his chance in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Landed a four-and-a-quarter-length success at Bath in April off an 8lb lower mark and has been running consistently since, including a staying-on second before her most recent outing — she was ridden patiently and left with too much to do over an inadequate trip last time and a return to a mile here looks ideal. Effective over 8f on a sound surface, Volendam is our top-rated runner and represents a strong each-way proposition back at her best distance.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Strong recent record on Good and Good-to-Soft (12/15 similar-going runs with 2 wins and 8 places) makes him one of the more interesting form entries in the field; Easterby has 10 winners from 103 in the last fortnight and the horse naturally wants to race prominently, but being pushed into a midfield slot by the race shape means he cannot fully express that style — his form figures still demand respect.
runners_data.comment: Landed a short-head success at Hamilton in May off a 1lb lower mark, Perfidia was running well throughout the season until a dismal outing last time where she found nothing under pressure — a sharp drop in performance that needs to be excused. Effective 7-8f on good ground, the mark is now back to her winning level and first-time headgear (p) is a positive; a key danger if returning to her earlier form.

runners_data.name: River Wharfe
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed forward on the map; all five recent runs have been on Standard and his one win in the last five came at 7f on Standard — Good ground and a likely controlled pace are both against him, and 58 days off adds to the questions.
runners_data.comment: Won earlier in the campaign but has been below that level since, including a poor effort at Southwell last time where he was never competitive — returning from a 58-day break on turf adds an element of the unknown. Effective 7-9f on any surface and from a wide draw in stall 8; a return to form is not out of the question but needs to be shown first.

races.paceDynamic: Rusheen Boy is the confirmed lone pace-setter and will take this field along from the front, likely uncontested on Good ground over 1m½f at Nottingham — a flat, fair track that allows a controlled front-runner to dictate entirely on their own terms. With no natural rival to press him through the early stages, Rusheen Boy can set a sustainable, metronomic tempo that keeps the race honest without burning himself out, making life genuinely difficult for hold-up types who need a strong injection of pace to close into. My Boy Harry and Mariner are both prominent-styled horses who should sit just off the leader, keeping the front-running shape intact rather than disrupting it. This field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Volendam and Perfidia are genuine prominent racers mapped to midfield because the positions ahead of them are occupied, while River Wharfe is a true hold-up type pushed further forward on the map than reality will allow; Rusheen Boy and My Boy Harry are most likely to actually secure the front positions. A controlled, single-leader race on Good turf over this stamina-testing mile-and-a-half strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can track the tempo and quicken late — true hold-up horses face an uphill task without a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rusheen Boy Leads, Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Rusheen Boy dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and the prominent trackers cannot sustain their challenge in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If Rusheen Boy dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and the prominent trackers cannot sustain their challenge in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Rusheen Boy's pace is sufficient to soften up the field but a prominent tracker conserves enough energy to reel him in close home.
scenarios.body: If Rusheen Boy's pace is sufficient to soften up the field but a prominent tracker conserves enough energy to reel him in close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a horse from a deeper position finds clear daylight in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a horse from a deeper position finds clear daylight in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closer Delivers Late Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens hard in the middle stages, burning off the prominent horses and leaving a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: If the pace unexpectedly quickens hard in the middle stages, burning off the prominent horses and leaving a gap for a late finisher.

watchPoints.text: Rusheen Boy is the sole pace-setter — if he gets any kind of bump or is crowded at the start by the prominent group, the entire race shape collapses and a more chaotic scenario opens up for trackers like My Boy Harry and Mariner.

Volendam and Perfidia are both genuine prominent horses who cannot all slot in behind Rusheen Boy; watch at the break to see who actually secures a position close to the pace and who gets shuffled back, as that will materially change each horse's chance.

Mbappe returns after 141 days off for a trainer with a 1/14 strike rate in the past fortnight — if visibly unfit or green in the parade ring, discount its chance regardless of the race shape that unfolds.

River Wharfe has run exclusively on Standard ground in all five recent starts — monitor the going report closely at the course; the declared Good is confirmed across multiple readings but any overnight change towards Soft would benefit his profile more than the current conditions suggest.

Bajan Bandit's 90-day absence combined with a form string of six 4th-6th finishes on Standard means any significant market move before the off should be noted — trainer P Morris is 1/8 in the past 14 days which is worth watching.

runners_data.name: Koodini
runners_data.comment: Produced a step forward at Chester last time, finishing second beaten three lengths under positive handling — the performance suggests he has more to offer and he is a player if building on it. Sired by a high-class miler out of a dam effective from 6f to a mile, the profile fits; yet to win, but shows enough to be the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Supreme Star
runners_data.comment: A Supremacy colt foaled in May who is a half-brother to Rebel At Dawn — a useful 6f performer — whose dam landed her second outing as a juvenile; an encouraging pedigree for a debut runner. Arrived at 4,000gns so market support will be key, but the family form gives reason to follow him in the betting.

runners_data.name: Ten Year Stretch
runners_data.comment: Struggled to lay up with the pace at Salisbury on debut, beaten seven lengths and never a factor — a sprint sire crossed with a middle-distance dam suggests the trip here may still not be long enough. Lightly raced and perhaps better over a stiffer test; not easy to back with confidence yet.

runners_data.name: Cheeky Chesca
runners_data.comment: Consistent in her first five appearances with three placed efforts, Cheeky Chesca was six lengths third at Hamilton most recently — she stays 6f and the quicker surface here plays to her strengths. The worry is that she has been knocking on the door without getting through; good enough to take a maiden on what she has shown, but the five-race blank is becoming a concern.

runners_data.name: Crowned
runners_data.comment: Caught a bit flat-footed early on debut at Windsor but picked up well in the closing stages to finish third, beaten three and a half lengths — the experience looks to have been instructive and a step up in trip should bring more. Effective at 5f and expected to stay further; yet to win but the debut read was encouraging.

runners_data.name: Emirates Express
runners_data.comment: Without a win in two recent starts, Emirates Express has had little to show and trailed home on both occasions without troubling a rival — the breeding suggests a mile may ultimately be the distance to unlock something, but there is nothing to go on at this stage. Best watched for now.

runners_data.name: Beechwood Glory
runners_data.comment: A Cotai Glory colt whose dam showed real ability at 6f as a juvenile, Beechwood Glory has a demanding introduction on debut and a yard not renowned for having runners ready first time — born in February, and youngsters with that profile often need the run. Worth monitoring but hard to fancy without a prep.

runners_data.name: Benefacta
runners_data.comment: Showed inexperience at Salisbury last time, hampered by the track and beaten eight lengths — still lightly raced and looks like she has further to develop. Effective over 6f on good to soft and possibly capable of staying a little further; the trainer is struggling for form at present, which adds a note of caution to an already tentative profile.

runners_data.name: Chan Noir
runners_data.comment: A Blackbeard colt — by a high-class sprinting sire out of a well-regarded middle-distance mare — Chan Noir fetched 32,000 guineas as a yearling and is a half-brother to Samurai Mike, who showed smart ability at 6f. With a pedigree that suggests 6f is likely to suit, the betting will be the guide on debut; hard to assess without a run.

races.name: Neigh More Early Starts For Martin Stoneman Handicap

runners_data.name: Return Of The Gods
runners_data.note: Pat Dobbs partners this 3yo for E Bethell who has one win from 21 runners over 14 days; a prominent runner on Good ground with three consecutive 6f runs at Southwell, the switch to Nottingham is unexplored but the style suits a fast-run race from the front.|
runners_data.comment: Strong 2yo form that has been well advertised since, Return Of The Gods was outpaced and needed the run on his handicap debut at Kempton, where he was never in contention — treated as a prep run. Yet to race on grass and trainer struggling for winners at present, but on his juvenile form he rates an unexposed threat; 78-day layoff is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Master Of Entropy
runners_data.note: J & S Quinn have had no winners from 14 runners in the past two weeks; this is a genuine hold-up horse whose last five runs are all over longer trips on soft or standard ground, and he now finds himself racing in a field too full of pace to get to the rear naturally — his best chance evaporates if he cannot settle off a true gallop.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard on his handicap debut at Chester on softer ground, a clearly unsuitable combination, and could be marked up for that — on what he has shown in maidens the mark looks fair. Effective over a mile on good and all-weather, Master Of Entropy is still learning the game; yet to win in recent starts but it is early in his career and draw 1 here.

runners_data.name: Space Bear
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — critical note: if Space Bear is a late withdrawal the entire race shape changes dramatically, removing the one confirmed pace-setter and collapsing the dominant scenario; check declarations; M Appleby's runner has won at 6f on Good and set up the map as it stands.|

runners_data.name: Cuban Lady
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's 4yo carries headgear and has won at 6f on Good ground, with five of her last five runs at that trip; Marco Ghiani takes over in the saddle and her prominent style fits perfectly into the space immediately behind the leader, making her one of the better-positioned horses in the field regardless of how hard the front end goes.|
runners_data.comment: Generally consistent and handles today's trip, Cuban Lady was fourth at Bath last time — running around freely early but building on her reappearance run. First-time cheekpieces could help settle matters, though without a win in recent starts and our figures ranking her fifth of six, she looks to need everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Fenlander
runners_data.note: Two wins from his last three starts at 6f on Good ground show this 5yo is in excellent form for Mrs P Sly, but the field is too loaded with prominent types for him to claim his natural front position — he will need to race from further back than ideal, and his STYLE_FIT tag reflects a genuine cost to his winning probability in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last five starts, Fenlander landed a four-length success at Leicester last time, pulling clear with plenty to spare off a 9lb lower mark — that improved form is the clearest piece of evidence in this field. Now up another 9lb, the question is whether he can keep progressing off the new ceiling; effective 5-6f on any ground.

runners_data.name: Emperor Caradoc
runners_data.note: P T Midgley's 7yo carries a hood, has three wins and five places from 15 runs on Good ground including a 6f win at this course, and is a reliable hold-up type; only nine days since his last run but that is not unusual for this profile, and he is the standout finisher in this field if pace is genuinely honest.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a half-length success off a 1lb lower mark at Thirsk in May and ran to that level again sixth last time at the same rating — same mark here now aided by first-time headgear (p). Effective at 5-6f on any ground, Emperor Caradoc is in decent shape and lines up as our top-rated runner; the chief query is whether he can translate consistent placed efforts into a win.

runners_data.name: Paws For Thought
runners_data.note: D McCain Jnr's 8yo is tagged as a horse who fades in the finish, and his recent form — 7th, 11th, 9th, 20th before a 1st on Soft — raises serious questions about consistency on Good ground at 6f; James Sullivan takes over but the fade flag makes him hard to trust even in a scenario that theoretically suits hold-up types.|
runners_data.comment: Progressed on reappearance but laboured to seventh without threatening at Chester last time, and the going here is likely to be quicker than this horse prefers — effective 5-7f but ideally wants some give. Suited to Chester's quirks, Paws For Thought looks hard to place here on fast ground and our figures put him last of six.

races.paceDynamic: Space Bear is the one confirmed front-runner and, with a clear lead, is set to control tempo from the gates at a sustainable but honest gallop over Nottingham's 6f straight. Cuban Lady, Return Of The Gods, and Fenlander are all prominent-type horses who will press forward and contest the early positions, meaning the lead group will be competitive rather than purely uncontested. This field holds more prominent and front-running types than the race can accommodate cleanly — Cuban Lady and Return Of The Gods are best placed to secure prominent berths behind Space Bear, while Fenlander and Master Of Entropy are genuine pace horses who will find themselves further back than their natural style dictates. A pressured but structured gallop suits hold-up horses who can finish off a truly-run 6f, with Emperor Caradoc the profile most likely to benefit if the leaders flatten out.

scenarios.title: Controlled lead, brave win
scenarios.trigger: If Space Bear dictates from the front, sets a fair but not suicidal pace, and holds on under pressure in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Space Bear dictates from the front, sets a fair but not suicidal pace, and holds on under pressure in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up types pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group press hard early and set a strong pace that drains Space Bear, allowing hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: If the prominent group press hard early and set a strong pace that drains Space Bear, allowing hold-up horses to sweep through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy pace, midfield chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types clash for position early and cause a scrappy, uneven tempo that disrupts the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent types clash for position early and cause a scrappy, uneven tempo that disrupts the race shape entirely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front group weakens, Fenlander delivers
scenarios.trigger: If Fenlander manages to work forward from a shuffled position and reclaims his natural prominent role as others tire.
scenarios.body: If Fenlander manages to work forward from a shuffled position and reclaims his natural prominent role as others tire.

watchPoints.text: Space Bear is a confirmed non-runner in the data — if confirmed absent, the sole pace-setter is gone and the race shape collapses entirely, redistributing advantage away from prominent types and toward hold-up horses like Emperor Caradoc.

Fenlander has won twice recently at 6f on Good but is mapped to midfield due to pace congestion — watch whether he can work forward early; if he cannot reclaim a prominent position, his strong recent form counts for little.

Emperor Caradoc has strong Good-ground form at this course and distance but is 9 days fresh; watch whether he settles cleanly in the hold-up position, as a flat 6f at Nottingham leaves little room for error if he misses the early flow.

Paws For Thought carries a fades-in-finish flag and has been out of the top three in four of his last five runs — his presence as a hold-up type in the rear group adds no real pace threat to the closers' scenario but could crowd Emperor Caradoc's run if they track similar ground.

races.name: Martin Stonemans Final Furlong Handicap

runners_data.name: Invincible Crown
runners_data.note: Trainer Mrs R Carr sends this 4yo in decent nick (9 days since last run) but recent form reads poorly — a run of 4th-6th-4th-7th on Good 5f turf tells a consistent midfield story; a genuine hold-up horse who will find himself unable to get as far back as he wants given the volume of closers in this field, which blunts his finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Met trouble in running and left with too much to do at Thirsk last time, beaten just one and a quarter lengths — a performance that should be marked up given the interference. Effective at 5f on a sound surface and a considerable way below her last winning mark, Invincible Crown has a chance if she gets a clear run; trainer cold at present, which is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Comedian Leader
runners_data.note: Six-year-old returning from a 97-day break for J & S Best, who are 0/4 in the last 14 days, and his entire recent form has come on Standard (AW) surfaces over longer trips — the switch back to Good turf at 5f makes the going and distance combination a live concern, and his natural desire to race from the rear will be compromised by the crowded hold-up quarter.
runners_data.comment: Finishing her last six starts between fifth and ninth, Comedian Leader has been held in recent outings — though she ran to form beaten two lengths at Lingfield last time at a 1lb higher mark. Races from off the pace, effective 6-8f on good ground and on a dropping mark after a short break; needs a sharp turn in fortunes to get involved here and is hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Doralee
runners_data.note: T D Barron has had two winners from 10 runners in the past fortnight, and this 5yo mare has the most relevant form in the race — three of her last five runs have been placed at 5f on Good turf, giving her an excellent sim-going record; as the most form-consistent of the closers, she is the likeliest of the hold-up trio to actually find her preferred late position.
runners_data.comment: Failed to land a blow at Ripon last time, beaten four and a half lengths without threatening — needs to reverse that trend to make an impact here. Effective at 5f on soft and good to firm, Doralee has a drop in weight over some rivals and has shown third-place consistency earlier in the season; hard to fancy with confidence until she reproduces that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Get Up Everybody
runners_data.note: Pat Midgley has two winners from 21 runners over 14 days and this 4yo has placed at 5f and 6f on Good ground, suggesting the conditions are fine; David Nolan is an experienced handler of tactical situations and this horse's ability to sit mid-division and pick up ground makes him a player if the early pace burns out the leaders.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Mayer
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner by headgear (previously gelded, cheekpieces noted) and the only horse in the field mapped as a genuine leader — Nicholas Tinkler sends him here 38 days fresh with a 3/26 14-day strike rate; although his sim-going record on Good turf is thin (2 wins, 6 places from 15), he gets a dream scenario with no pace rival to duel with.
runners_data.comment: Below his best in recent outings — beaten five and a half lengths at Redcar last time — Sergeant Mayer's mark has been easing as a result, which offers some potential upside. Effective 5-6f on good to soft and fast ground, and first-time headgear (p) may help; without a win in recent starts and form hard to trust, though a better mark could tempt.

runners_data.name: Irish Dancer
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Good turf and placed twice on the same surface, making him the best-credentialled prominent racer in this field on today's conditions — Zak Wheatley takes the ride for D Carroll, who is 2/19 over 14 days, and the tongue-tie is retained; tracking Sergeant Mayer in second is a near-certain outcome and his recent 1 places him as a genuine contender in the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: Took a half-length success at Catterick three starts back off a 2lb lower mark and ran to that level again when a short-head second most recently — same mark applies today with first-time headgear (tb) added. Irish Dancer is generally consistent at 5f on a range of surfaces; the mark looks high enough, but with recent placed efforts this is a leading danger to our selection.

runners_data.name: Beerwah
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani rides for J & S Quinn (0 from 10 in 14 days) and this 4yo wore a hood last time, when finishing second on Good 5f ground — he has a win and four placings from his last five runs on Good turf and has course form, making him the most complete hold-up/chasing horse in the race if the prominent pair tire; 20 days since last run is a comfortable gap.
runners_data.comment: Took a one-and-a-quarter-length success at Redcar three starts back and was poorly positioned in a race run at a strong pace from the front last time — that sixth is best set aside. First-time blinkers added today and effective at 5f on fast and soft ground, Beerwah is our top-rated runner; form has been patchy of late and the rating looks demanding, but the equipment change could sharpen the picture.

races.paceDynamic: Sergeant Mayer is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 5f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him from the gates, he is able to dictate at a sustainable gallop from the front. Irish Dancer will push up prominently in pursuit, sitting just off the leader's hip and ensuring the early tempo is honest without becoming a true burning pace. The three hold-up types — Invincible Crown, Comedian Leader, and Doralee — are true closers by nature but the field has too many horses wanting the rear for all to settle there comfortably; Doralee, with the sharpest recent 5f form on Good ground, is best placed to secure a genuine hold-up berth, while Invincible Crown and Comedian Leader are likely to be squeezed into a closer mid-division position than ideal. On Good ground over a flat 5f at Nottingham with a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured pace, this race shape heavily favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the final furlong rather than those needing a truly compressed, late-injection finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch Sergeant Mayer's draw and early break — if he gains a clean passage to the rail uncontested, the race could effectively be won before the quarter-pole as no horse in this field has the pace to chase him down from the gates.

Comedian Leader's 97-day absence and recent runs exclusively on AW over longer trips make him a significant unknown on Good turf; if he shapes poorly early it confirms the going and trip are against him and he can be sidelined from calculations.

Doralee, Invincible Crown, and Comedian Leader cannot all find their natural hold-up position — watch in the first furlong whether one or two of them are forced to race closer to the pace than intended, which would compromise any of their late runs.

Irish Dancer is fitted with a tongue-tie and has been off only 9 days — watch how quickly Zak Wheatley commits him to press Sergeant Mayer, as an aggressive move to claim second slot early locks in his tactical advantage for the entire race.

Beerwah's hood is absent today having worn one last time when finishing second — watch whether he settles cleanly in the early stages, as headgear removal can affect a horse's concentration and alter its natural racing pattern.
